**[goal]**
Close H1 2026 for the investor/board meeting: derive monthly revenue, gross margin and EBITDA (Jan–Jun), then cash burn and runway, and save the key figures to `./result.json`.

**[action]**
Read the four files in `./finance`: the ledger (86 entries, `date;account;description;amount`, Brazilian format where `.` is thousands and `,` is decimal), the chart of accounts (maps each account to a P&L line), the cash balance note, and the board's README. Aggregated ledger amounts by month and P&L line, then applied the board's definitions. Wrote and cross-checked with a second, independent parser; both produced identical numbers.

**[result]**
CFO summary (R$, Jan–Jun 2026):

| Month | Revenue | Gross margin | EBITDA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jan | 200,510.87 | 70.03% | −210,278.96 |
| Feb | 216,328.06 | 70.29% | −212,300.08 |
| Mar | 219,066.17 | 68.46% | −204,525.45 |
| Apr | 238,163.26 | 70.24% | −196,950.65 |
| May | 243,032.89 | 69.56% | −201,945.82 |
| Jun | 272,391.57 | 72.41% | −192,968.22 |

Story: revenue up ~36% across the half (200.5k → 272.4k); gross margin steady in a healthy 68–72% band; EBITDA negative every month but narrowing — monthly loss improved from ~210k to ~193k. Burn = R$197,288.23/month (average negative EBITDA of the last three closed months, Apr–Jun). Runway = 9.36 months on the 30/06 cash of R$1,847,350.40, i.e. cash lasts to roughly mid-April 2027 at this burn. All keys are in `./result.json`.

Assumptions: amounts parsed as BRL; revenue is net of refunds (3.1.09 kept as negative); gross margin = (revenue + COGS)/revenue with COGS stored negative; EBITDA sums revenue, COGS, sales & marketing, R&D and G&A, excludes the non-operating "financial" line (investment income, interest/IOF) and notes no D&A accounts exist; "last three closed months" = Apr–Jun before the 30/06 balance date; burn reported as a positive consumption rate; dates are dd/mm/yyyy. Caveat to flag to the CFO: actual cash fell R$461,837.60 in June (2,309,188.00 → 1,847,350.40), well above June's EBITDA loss of R$192,968.22 — the board-defined runway is EBITDA-based and therefore optimistic if that cash drop reflects recurring outflows not in the ledger.

**[next]**
No open tabs or apps to close. If the CFO wants the cash-based runway instead, I can recompute it from observed monthly cash movement and add it to `result.json`.

**What I found and why it is right:** revenue, gross margin and EBITDA for all six months plus burn of R$197,288.23 and runway of 9.36 months, recorded in `./result.json`. I know it is right because I reproduced every figure with two independent parsing/aggregation implementations and reconciled the EBITDA build-up (gross profit less opex, financial line excluded) against each month's ledger lines.

answers:
[goal]
Fix the `arena_scores` scoreboard crate so the match server stops hanging and final scores stop coming out low, without changing its public API, the tests in `./tests`, or adding dependencies.

[action]
Root-caused two concurrency defects in `src/lib.rs` and fixed both in place:

- `award` read a value with one lock, released it, then wrote back with a second lock (same for `total`). Two threads could read the same value and overwrite each other, losing points. Replaced with `+=` under a single lock guard per value, so the read-modify-write is atomic.
- `transfer` locked the two player slots in call order. A self-transfer (`from == to`) locked one mutex twice, and two threads transferring in opposite directions locked A-then-B and B-then-A. Both deadlock. Added an early return for `from == to` and acquire both slots in a fixed order by `PlayerId`, keeping the move atomic and preserving "total does not change".

Temporary stress tests were used to reproduce the bugs and verify the fix, then deleted; `./tests` contains only the original `board.rs`.

[result]
- Original code, award stress test: `left: 15992, right: 16000` (points lost), test FAILED.
- Original code, transfer test: hung past 12s timeout (deadlock).
- Fixed code, both stress tests: ok.
- `cargo test` final: `test one_thread_keeps_the_scores ... ok`, 1 passed, 0 failed.

[next]
Assumptions: a player joins once (rejoin/overwrite semantics in `join` were left as-is, since the brief and tests do not define it); `transfer` must remain atomic as a pair and keep the total unchanged, as documented; no new dependencies and no public API or test changes. No browser tabs, windows, or apps were opened.

What I found and how I know it is right: the hangs were deadlocks in `transfer` (self-transfer double-lock and opposing-transfer lock-order inversion), and the low scores were lost updates in `award` from releasing the lock between read and write. I know this because I reproduced each failure against the original code with recorded evidence (15992 vs 16000 points; a 12s hang), then showed both pass after the fix, and confirmed the unchanged `./tests` suite still passes.

Deliverable: result.json and the page are in place, but the run timed out with no final message, so there is no account of findings, assumptions or limits. words.json uses slugs rather than words, inconsistently accented.
